analysis.investment_thesis: Astra Microwave fails the Magic Formula on its most critical input: earnings yield is a meager ~2.5% (EBIT ₹269 Cr / EV ~₹10,781 Cr), far below the 12% threshold, meaning you are paying a steep premium for future earnings that haven't materialized in free cash. ROIC of ~17% is adequate but not exceptional enough to justify a 64x P/E when cash generation is persistently negative.
key_strengths: Improving operating margins — EBIT grew from ₹77 Cr (2021) to ₹269 Cr (2025), a genuine operational ramp-up in a high-barrier defense niche
Captive demand moat — defense/space/EW subsystems have limited domestic competition and long government program lifetimes
Revenue CAGR of 11.1% over 9 years with accelerating momentum in the last 3 years
key_risks: Chronically negative FCF — OCF was negative in 4 of last 5 years (FY25: -₹90 Cr), meaning reported earnings are NOT converting to cash; working capital trap is severe
Valuation is punishing — EV/EBITDA of 36x and earnings yield of ~2.5% leave zero margin of safety; any earnings miss or order delay could crater the stock
Finance costs doubling (₹32 Cr → ₹57 Cr in one year) as debt climbs to ₹424 Cr, eroding the quality of earnings growth
red_flags: Earnings yield ~2.5% — catastrophically below the Magic Formula's 12% minimum; stock is not cheap by any EBIT-based measure
Free cash flow negative ₹169 Cr in FY25 despite ₹154 Cr net profit — a massive ₹323 Cr divergence signals aggressive working capital build or revenue recognition ahead of cash collection
Promoter holding of only 6.54% is alarmingly low for a defense-tech company — almost no founder skin in the game
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Astra Microwave produces a poor result on both axes. Earnings Yield: EBIT of ₹269 Cr against an Enterprise Value of ~₹10,781 Cr (market cap ₹10,382 Cr + net debt ₹399 Cr) yields just 2.5% — less than a government bond, and roughly one-fifth of the 12% threshold I look for. Return on Capital: using invested capital of ~₹1,562 Cr (equity + debt - cash), ROIC comes to ~17%, which is adequate but not the 25%+ quality I want in a Magic Formula name. The business ranks in the bottom quartile on cheapness and middle quartile on quality — a combination that the formula historically underperforms.

The deeper problem is cash generation. Net profit has grown nicely to ₹154 Cr in FY25, but operating cash flow was -₹90 Cr and free cash flow was -₹169 Cr. This pattern — positive income, deeply negative cash — has repeated in 4 of the last 5 years and signals either an aggressive revenue recognition cycle or a working capital model where government receivables pile up for years. Defense companies often have lumpy collections, but this level of divergence is a structural concern, not a timing quirk. Until earnings translate reliably into cash, the 64x P/E is pricing perfection with no cushion for delays.
